summary: This note is a short biography of Wee Willie Smith, a 6'5" African American basketball player considered one of the first great African American players. It covers his semi-professional start in the Cleveland area, his years with the New York Renaissance, his later professional play including the Cleveland Chase Brassmen, and his life and honors after basketball.
one_line: Wee Willie Smith was a 6'5" pioneering African American basketball player who starred with the New York Renaissance in the 1930s.
key_facts: Wee Willie Smith was 6'5" and was one of the first great African American basketball players.
Smith played for several semi-professional leagues in the Cleveland, Ohio area before joining the New York Renaissance in 1932.
The New York Renaissance was described as an all-black professional team.
From 1932 to 1936, Smith and his six teammates won over 400 games.
The Renaissance won an 88-game winning streak from January 1, 1933 to March 27, 1933.
The entire 1932–33 New York Renaissance team was collectively inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 1963.
Wee Willie Smith played for the Cleveland Chase Brassmen of the National Basketball League.
Wee Willie Smith was one of the few black players in the history of the National Basketball League.
After basketball, Wee Willie Smith worked as a custodian in the Cleveland Public Schools.
After basketball, Wee Willie Smith operated a beverage shop.
Wee Willie Smith was inducted into the Harlem Hall of Fame in 1977.
Wee Willie Smith was inducted into the Greater Cleveland Sports Hall of Fame in 1977.
